answer: Give every agent one US Coast Guard Merchant Mariner Credential, verified against the National Maritime Center database. A real MMC costs $140 in fees plus a $95 TWIC card, a medical exam, and sea time that cannot be bought overnight; a forger must forge the credential, the TWIC, and the sea-service record together. At dawn the registry check runs again: any mismatch freezes the agent's escrow and burns its stake, so a thousand fake mariners need a thousand fake careers. The ridge between a real sailor and a bot is paperwork the sea itself witnessed.
